1 Introduction

1.1 Purpose

This document is the system architecture and design report of My Project. It presents the SysML model as numbered, printable diagrams and tables: package structure, requirements, use cases, block and internal block structure, parametrics, behaviour and the requirements traceability matrix.

1.2 Scope

The report covers canonical model revision 0 as generated on 2026-10-08 12:05 UTC. Every diagram reports the connections it could not draw; they are collected in Appendix A.

9.2 Corner Case & Behaviour Analysis

Systematic audit of risk-prone states, deadlock conditions, race risks, and boundaries in the designed logic.

IDCategorySeverityElementDescriptionRecommendation
CC-001deadlockCRITICALBState "B" and all its ancestors have no outgoing transitions, and it is not marked as a safe-state or terminal state. The system will be trapped here permanently.Add an outgoing transition from State 'B' or mark it as an intentional terminal state in the model.
CC-002missing_actionINFOAState "A" has transitions but no entry, during, or exit actions defined. It is a pass-through state with no observable behavior.Add at least an entry or during action, or document why this state is intentionally passive.
CC-003missing_actionINFOBState "B" has transitions but no entry, during, or exit actions defined. It is a pass-through state with no observable behavior.Add at least an entry or during action, or document why this state is intentionally passive.

9.3 Test Scenario Matrix

Structurally derived test scenarios for critical paths and detected corner cases. Execute them in host, differential, embedded, and target-hardware gates before treating them as runtime evidence.

CRITICAL_PATH Walk-through: Critical Path 1: A → B TS-001
Preconditions:
  • System is powered on and SM_Init() has been called
  • count = 1
  • go = false
  • ratio = 0
  • total = 0
StepAction / input stimulusExpected transition / output state
1Call SM_Init() to enter autostart stateSystem enters state "A"
2Set variables to satisfy [go], then call SM_Step(&instance, SM_TICK_MS)System transitions from "A" to "B"
Expected outcome: System reaches terminal state "B" without crashes or assertion failures.
CORNER_CASE Corner Case: deadlock — B TS-002
Preconditions:
  • SM_Init() called
  • System in known good state
StepAction / input stimulusExpected transition / output state
1Navigate the system to state "B"System is in state "B"
2Call SM_Step(&instance, SM_TICK_MS) repeatedly (100 ticks)System remains in "B" — verify no memory corruption or watchdog timeout
3Verify SM_GetActiveSlot() or SM_GetLayerActive() returns expected enumActive state is SM_ST_B
Expected outcome: System handles the deadlock gracefully with no crash, hang, or undefined behavior.

Appendix B Glossary of SysML notation

Table 7 — Notation used in this report
SymbolNameMeaning
«block»BlockA modular unit of system structure; compartments list its properties, operations and ports.
PartPart propertyA usage of a block inside another block, drawn as a box in an internal block diagram. Written name : Type [multiplicity].
Small squarePortAn interaction point on a block or part. Position follows the flow direction where it is declared.
Solid line with arrowConnector / item flowLinks two ports or parts; the label names the item that flows along it.
Filled diamondCompositionThe whole owns the part; the part cannot outlive the whole.
Hollow diamondAggregationThe whole references shared parts.
Hollow triangleGeneralizationPoints from the specific element to the general one.
Dashed arrowDependencyLabelled with its keyword, for example «satisfy», «verify», «refine», «deriveReqt», «trace», «allocate».
Circle with crossContainmentA requirement contains the requirements nested under it.
Orange outlineRequirementA statement of need with an identifier, text, status and priority.
Ellipse / stick figureUse case / actorA use case lives inside its subject boundary; actors stand outside. «include» and «extend» are dashed.
Rounded box, barsActivityActions with control flow (solid) and object flow (dashed); decision/merge diamonds, fork/join bars; swimlanes are partitions.
Lifeline, arrowsSequenceMessages run top to bottom: filled head = synchronous call, open head = asynchronous, dashed = reply. Frames are combined fragments (alt, opt, loop, par).
Rounded rectangle with squaresConstraint propertyA parametric constraint; the small squares are its parameters, bound to value properties by binding connectors.
Rounded state boxStateShows entry / during / exit actions. A container box holds sub-states; a linked state has its own subsection.
[guard] / actionTransition labelThe transition fires when the guard holds and then runs the action; after(n) is a timed trigger.
H, H*HistoryShallow and deep history pseudostates.
S V R D TGrid glyphsRequirement to element grid: satisfy, verify, refine, derive, trace.
